justification: Automatic renewal and no-further-confirmation billing are buried in nested Terms details at DOM depth 6 and in tiny text.
s0 places an automatic-renewal/charge-without-confirmation clause in collapsed nested details at DOM=6; Hidden Information #3 and Complex Language #1 fire, and E2 does not cover collapsed disclosure.
A visibly marked AD card uses ‘Continue reading’ and a full-width ‘Next’ button beside the article, making an advertisement look like native continuation; s1 calls it a semantic masquerade.
s0-s1 show the AD card using native-looking ‘Next’/‘Continue reading’; Disguised Ad #3 semantic mimicry is observed, but the destination domain is not in the trace, so confidence is limited.
The consent prompt says consent registers automatically after a two-second window, offers no working customization or decline path, and disappears in the final state.
s1 shows timed consent with a 1.0-second window and automatic registration if idle; the prompt is gone in s2. Automating The User Away #3, O6, and the absent opt-out path fire.
Every state repeats ‘Hurry,’ ‘ends soon,’ and ‘don’t risk missing out’; requests for the exact end time receive only evasive answers such as ‘Very soon!’ and ‘cannot disclose.’
s0-s3 repeat high-pressure scarcity while the answer states never provide a concrete deadline; Limited Time Message #3 fires because specificity is absent and E4 does not apply.
The checkout shows a checked optional $2 donation and includes it in the $131.99 total without any shown user choice.
s0 has a checked optional donation before any user event; s1 confirms it was checked at mount and folded into the total without consent. O5 and Sneak Into Basket #3 fire.
The offer uses a red-orange hue, ‘Only today — ends in 4 hours,’ and ‘Don’t miss it’/double-price pressure to push immediate purchase.
s0-s1 show a specific four-hour deadline, not an unbounded or fabricated timer; although Limited Time Message #2’s color/text condition is visible, E4’s real-deadline escape clause applies.
After Add to Cart, the cart jumps from one product to three, adding a warranty and priority shipping that were never selected; later states expose removal controls.
s0→s1 changes one selected product into three cart items, adding a warranty and priority shipping without a user event; s2-s3 remove them. Sneak Into Basket #1 is directly corroborated.
Accept all is one prominent action, while rejecting requires individually switching off 24 partners and there is explicitly no reject-all control.
s0-s1 make acceptance one click but provide no Reject all; opt-out requires 24 individual controls. Privacy Maze #1 and O3’s opt-out asymmetry fire; unchecked boxes do not trigger O5.
Entering cancellation adds a large sad puppy and ‘Don’t leave us…’ before the user can confirm cancellation, using guilt to retain the subscription.
s0→s1 injects a large sad puppy only in the cancellation flow with ‘Don’t leave us…’; Cuteness #1-#3 and guilt proximity fire despite a visible cancel button.
Accept All is a large filled button with shadow, while the alternative is a small, quiet underlined Manage options link.
s0 gives Accept All a full-width 12px/py-3 filled treatment and Manage options a 9px text-link treatment; False Hierarchy #2/Privacy Maze visual disparity fires under E1’s relative comparison.
The deletion confirmation uses FINAL, GONE FOREVER, NEVER, REGRET, and MISS language to shame the user, while the delete choice is visually weaker.
s0-s1 pair intense guilt/shame copy with a smaller outlined delete choice versus the large keep-account button; Confirmshaming #2 fires even though both controls remain available under O3.
The creator says that failing to raise $5 will end the channel for good, directly pressuring viewers beside the tip buttons.
s0 asserts that $0 support causes the creator’s channel to fail and places that claim beside tip prompts; Parasocial Pressure #1 fires. s1 records only a preview, not payment.
The initial state requires an explicit Play click, and s1’s event log records that click before playback begins; no autonomous start is shown.
s0 has a clear Play control and s1 explicitly logs ‘User clicked Play’; Auto-Play #1 is refuted, with no autonomous execution or suppressed start vector observed.
The offer repeats ‘only 3 left,’ ‘selling fast,’ ‘ends soon,’ ‘last chance,’ and ‘don’t miss out’ without giving a concrete end time.
s0-s1 repeat dense scarcity language and provide no concrete deadline or timer; Limited Time Message #3 and FOMO #3 fire. Stock fabrication itself is unobservable, but is not needed for the verdict.
A struck $299 MSRP anchors the $149 price and is paired with ‘Save 50% — today only’; the later state identifies the anchor as fabricated.
s0-s1 show $299 above a struck-through $149 and state1 reports a fabricated MSRP/2.01 anchor ratio; Reference Pricing #3 fires, even though the discount is only 50%.
Only a shallow Account settings accordion is exposed; the fragment never shows a harmful target, an excessive path, or unrelated labels, so the apparent nesting is insufficient evidence.

s0-s3 expose only Account settings and one 12px-indented level (General, Billing, Notifications); no target path, >4 depth, or semantically unrelated link is observed, so Labyrinthine conditions fail.
The single state shows an ordinary, clearly labeled hold-to-refresh control and no pressure, hidden choice, or suspicious reward behavior.

s0 shows only a standard pull-to-refresh affordance; no refresh sequence, artificial delay, variable reward, or missing control is observable. Pull-To-Refresh conditions are unverified and E5 limits confidence.
The interface presents two plainly labeled tracking choices, I accept and No, I don’t accept, with comparable button treatment.
s0 presents explicit, mutually opposite tracking buttons with no preselection or label mismatch; O5 is negative and no ontology condition fires.
The annual plan is priced only as 2,990 Coins, and the interface says its real-money value is never stated even when asked for PLN.
s0-s1 show 2,990 Coins and explicitly report convert(...)=none with no PLN/USD/EUR mapping; Price Comparison Prevention #1 and Intermediate Currency #2 fire.
The fragment shows a conventional three-tier referral-reward program but no blocked core feature, mass invite action, or unconsented side effect.
s0-s1 expose reward intensities 1→3→9 and escalating ‘exclusive,’ ‘premium,’ and ‘Circle’ language; Social Pyramid #3 fires, although core gating in #1 is absent.
Account deletion is scheduled 30 days after the request rather than performed immediately, with no visible cancellation or reversal control.
s1-s2 schedule deletion 30 days/720 hours after submission, provide no cancel or reversal affordance in any state, and call the delay programmatic; Forced Grace Period #1/#3 and O6 fire.
The clickable scare-copy says ‘Act now’ and ‘Don’t miss out’; the later state reports six listeners on that coercive text versus one on neutral text.
s0-s1 show coercive text in a role=button and report 6 listeners versus 1 (6/1=6, above the displayed threshold 3); Persuasive Language #1/#2 fire.
Sharing data with advertising partners starts enabled and prominent, while the essential-only alternative is smaller, dimmed, and off.
s0 preloads the advertising-partner switch on while the required-only switch is off, opacity-dimmed, and smaller; Bad Defaults #1/#3 and Privacy Zuckering #2 fire under O5.
Account settings explicitly says No exit and exposes only profile, privacy, and data/storage sections, with no delete, deactivate, or close control.
s0-s1 retain the ‘No exit’ state and show no deletion/offboarding keyword or control in the settings DOM; Immortal Accounts #3 and O6 fire.
The full-width, shadowed renewal button dominates a tiny underlined cancel link, which is paired with loss-of-access pressure despite the renewal price being shown.
s0-s1 give renewal a large 12px/py-3.5 filled button and cancel an 8px text link with loss framing; False Hierarchy #2/#3 fire. The pre-commit disclosure satisfies E2 only for hidden-fee claims.
The cookie overlay leaves only Accept all and provides no visible close, cancel, skip, or settings escape.
s1 identifies a z-index 1000 overlay with an empty dismissal set and no controls; Dead End #2 and O6 fire because only the compliance path exists.
Four glowing five-star testimonials all come from Guest user/Unverified · no profile, making their provenance unverifiable.
s0-s1 show four five-star cards with no full name, photo, or linked profile; state1 confirms the absence. Endorsement and Testimonials #2 fires.
The player is already marked playing and will advance to the next episode in 8 seconds; stopping requires using the corner pause control rather than a normal play/pause flow.

s0 is already playing and announces ‘Next episode in 8s’ with no play event or explicit autoplay wording; Auto-Play #1/#3 are plausible, but the single-state behavior is unobservable and E5 caps confidence at 0.6.
After the user starts the video, a sponsored ad takes over and its ‘Skip in 15s’ control is visibly disabled with no close option.
s0 Play video leads to s1’s Sponsored ad with disabled Skip in 15s and no close control; Countdown On Ads #1/#2 and O6 fire.
A shared cooperative study session is reframed as ‘You vs. Alex,’ with a loser demotion threat that pressures competition.
s0-s3 render the cooperative session as a You-vs-Alex split with opposing progress bars and loser demotion; Encouraging Anti-Social Behavior #2 fires.
The account interface is in English, but the cancellation confirmation and both decision buttons switch to German.
s0 acquisition/settings text is English; s1 termination confirmation is German despite the English session. Wrong Language #1/#3 fire.
The sword cannot be bought by card: the user must first exchange fiat for Gems, then pay in the virtual currency.
s0 disables purchase until exchange, s1 exposes Pay 2,500 Gems, and s2 records exchange executed while card payment is forbidden; Intermediate Currency #1/#3 fire.
The feed appends stories as the user scrolls and explicitly says there is no Load More button or endpoint.
s0→s3 grows the feed from 8 to 12 items with Loading more posts and no Load More/end marker; Infinite Scrolling #1/#3 fire.
The reader uses visible Previous/Next controls, with content changing only when those controls are used; no autonomous feed growth or hidden commitment is shown.

s0-s3 change only between two visible pages via Previous/Next, keep the controls available, and show no autonomous append, unreachable footer, or reward loop; Infinite Scrolling/Addictive conditions fail.
The plan presents 30 paid add-on choices in a dense grid and requires the user to review them all, creating clear choice overload.
s0-s3 present 30 actionable add-on buttons, exceeding Choice Overload #1’s displayed >20 threshold; the options being optional and priced does not remove the overload condition.
Contact access is framed as ‘Find your friends’ and ‘Let your contacts know you’re here,’ with a single Allow & find friends action and no skip path.
s0 frames address-book access as a social benefit to third parties; Address Book Leeching #3 fires. Core blocking and invite-all behavior are unobserved, so confidence remains moderate.
The page claims others are buying now, while its visible backend event log has zero entries and says no transactions were found.
s0 directly contrasts ‘Others are buying right now’ with real(t)=0 and no records; High Demand #1’s displayed-versus-true metric mismatch fires.
